title: The Hollow Oak
text: An oak so old it has gone hollow, its trunk as wide as a cottage, its branches holding up half the sky. Someone lives inside. Smoke curls from a knothole. The door is a knot in the bark, and on it hangs a little wreath of teeth.

options.label: Knock on the door with the wreath of teeth, and hope for a kind host.

outcomes.text: An old hermit answers, glad of company. He feeds you, but does not say whose teeth they were.
It is not a hermit who answers.

options.label: The quietest peeks in through the knothole, before anyone knocks.

outcomes.text: Inside lies a hoard of acorns, one of them gold.

options.label: Let whoever lives there be. Teeth on a door are warning enough.

outcomes.text: Eyes in the knot follow you, and a small voice wishes you well. It seems to mean it, for the road is gentle afterward.
